To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
federated learning is possible for training neural networks, and that model averaging over multiple clients is surprisingly effective.
federated learning can train deep networks with surprisingly little communication, and that the key to this is to average the models computed by the different devices.

(1) federated averaging is an effective algorithm for learning models from data distributed across many devices; (2) federated averaging works well even when the data is non-IID, which is the typical case for mobile devices; and (3) federated averaging can be used to train models that have many more parameters than the amount of data available on each device.
